about: How Outrigger treats each FM-1 firmware family, keyed by mutant.cloud firmware.json's `base`. Reviewed by hand: a listing's base is self-serve on mutant.cloud, so blocked_ids here override it. cleared_ids: Felucca 0.9 and SLOOP forks whose flash driver, read at the listed release tag, erases and writes only inside the clean slate (0x94000-0xE8FFF, 0xFC000-0xFEFFF); they beat a blocked base, and firmwares built on them are not blocked by them. A new release of one needs its map read again. tools/gen_families.py turns this and tools/fm1_lineage.json into the loader's lib/fm1_loader/src/families_gen.h and the Add firmware page's site/installer/families_gen.js. hub_ids: mutant.cloud entries the Hub (and boards' shelves) know by another id, matched by repo. docs/firmware-catalog.md explains the groups.

cleared_ids.hortator: drum-v1.0.1: writes only 0x97000-0xDFFFF, 0xE0000-0xE4FFF, 0xFC000-0xFEFFF; its Bluetooth never writes the radio's sector

mutant_says.mycelium: the Hub says Felucca and SLOOP; mutant.cloud says Felucca
